newsitem.title: FRANCE: Full text of Alcatel H1 results statement.
newsitem.headline: Full text of Alcatel H1 results statement.

text.p: Following is the full text of the Alcatel Alsthom first half results' statement.

"On September 25, 1996, Serge Tchuruk, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, presented the first half 1996 results and reported the progress on Alcatel Alsthom's recovery plan to the Board of Directors."

"During the first half, the Group registered income from operations of 0.5 billion francs compared with 1.4 billion francs in the first half of 1995 and a net loss of 0.4 billion compared with a loss of 1.2 billion in the corresponding period of 1995."

"The Board of Directors noted that the results were in line with the action program and reflected the recent trends amd the still limited effects of the current recovery plan. The Board also noted that the effects of the plan, already noticable for the second half, enabled the Group to aim at a return to break-even for the whole year and to foresee a significant reduction in debt, taking into account the divestments already completed as of today."
RESULTS AT JUNE 30, 1996

"At the same time, the Telecom sector's activities have been repositioned towards high growth market segments thanks to a competitive product portfolio particularly adopted to the most recent market trends."

"Activities during the first half were characterised by numerous commercial successes which, despite the market fall in undersea cables, resulted in a global increase of 3.8 percent in orders, which reached 81.5 billion francs. The growth was particularly strong in the Telecom sector."

"Sales during the first half, which mainly reflected delivery of orders received in 1995, amounted to 74.3 billion francs, a decrease of 3.4 percent over the same period in 1995, on a comparable basis."
"Income from operations amounted to 0.5 billion francs compared to 1.4 billion during the first half of 1995."
"This decrease comes from the Telecoms sector for 0.6 billion and the Cables sector for 0.3 billion."

"The Telecom sector's income from operations (-1.1 billion), declined compared to the first half (1995 - 0.5 billion). However, it shows an improvement over the second half 1995 (-2.8 billion or -1.3 billion excluding exceptional items) and should return to a postive level for the second half."
"Income from operations in the Cables sector amounted to 0.9 billion francs. The decrease compared to the first half 1995 is due to the strong deterioration in the undersea cable activities.

"GEC Alsthom maintained its income from operations at 0.6 billion francs at the same level as in the first half of 1995, within the context of a power generation market still characterised by intense competition. Orders increased during the first half and major achievements were recorded in the rail transportation activities, notable in North America."

"Income from operations in the "Systems" activities, while negative, did improve. The loss recorded in income from operations is entirely due to the integration of Alcatel Siete where restructuring is satisfactorily progressing."
"Saft registered income from operations at approximately the same level as that of the first half 1995. The activities continue to grow, particularly in the high potential technological markets."
"The increase of 0.8 billion in net income, is mainly due to a reduction in income tax and an increase in net income of equity affiliates."

"During the first half and income tax credit of 0.1 billion was registered compared with a charge of 1.3 billion during the first half 1995. This difference is partly due to a decrease in income from consolidated companies, but mainly reflects an improved management of the Group's worldwide tax position, and the effects of recognizing tax consolidation in th year in which it occured, in compliance with international accounting standards."

"In addition, net income of equity affiliates, which include notably the results of Havas, Framatome, Shanghia Bell, and Cofira (after exceptional items), increased from 0.1 billion in the first half 1995 to 0.8 billion in the first half 1996."
PROGRESS OF THE RECOVERY PLAN
"The plan announced a few months ago is progressing according to expectations."

"Half of the 10 billion asset disposal program has been achieved. It should be completed in the coming months, which will result in a substantial reduction of the debt to equity ratio. This refocusing is complemented by the simplification of the Group's legal structure wherein the number of legal entities has already been reduced by more than 300, representing a third of the previous count."
"The objective of achieving global savings of 7.0 billion francs per year by 1998 is maintained."

"Restructuring measures, mainly concerning the Telecoms and Cable sectors, have become indispensable due to the radical changes occuring in the Group's economic environment. Since mid-1995, close to 20,000 job reduction, principally in Europe, have been announced or realized in these two sectors. The subsequent plans seeks all possible solutions to reclassify affected employees."

Simultaniously, the Group has began a program to significantly reduce (by 10 billion francs) its gross operating assets as well as its administrative expenses which could allow annual savings of over 2.0 billion francs."
TELECOM ACTIVITIES
"The Group's Telecommunications activities sector has undergone significant changes during the last months, which deserve a special mention."

"The first half 1996 was characterised by a clear resumption in orders (+21 percent) and of sales (+5 percent) despite a decrease in switching, which is due to a drop in prices, the shrinkage of some major markets, in particular France, and the significant decrease in exports to China, where local production has considerably increased."
"To respond, the Group has reinforced its software and service offerings in switching for it to remain one of the major key elements of Alcatel's portfolio."

"Conversely, the product portfolio is undergoing significant transformation, favoring sector with high growth potential: transmission, access systems, data netwroks, mobile infrastructure. Orders and sales will progress by more than 40 percent in 1996 in the field of transmission. This development is especially accelerating in the U.S. where sales have doubled over the last four years, passing the one billion dollar treshold this year."
"Similarly, in access systems, where the market is expanding strongly (+ 20 percent per year) Alcatel will also register a growth in its orders and sales of over 40 percent in 1996."

"The strategy of alliances and partnerships is being pursued, through cooperations with Sharp in the mobile handset activities, and with the signing of an agreement with Motorola regarding mobile communications infrastructure (CDMA and DECT standards) and for the cross supply of equipment".
"All of these actions together should allow the Telecom business to regain a significant growth rate in the coming years (+5 to +10 percent per year)."
